content.text: Section 8 fully satisfies the preferred position, and no conflicting renewal or uplift language exists elsewhere.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Clause 8.2 provides automatic twelve-month (not multi-year) renewals that Customer may exit on only thirty days' written notice, with a Vendor reminder sixty days before renewal — and an extension of the opt-out deadline if the reminder is not sent, which is better than our preferred mechanic. Clause 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. Section 7 fixes Fees during the initial term and contains no competing escalation right, and Section 4 adds no renewal terms. This meets the preferred position on every material term (renewal term length, notice window, reminder, uplift cap); no redline needed.
